# Commercial drone architecture index

Canonical B2 product documentation: <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage>.

Use this index to choose a workflow. Each linked architecture states its data flow, B2 zones, boundaries, and security model.

## [Offload flight captures into a per-mission archive and trigger processing](../architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md)

After each flight, a field laptop, ground station or relay uploads stills, video, telemetry, flight logs and RTK/PPK files into a write-once per-mission prefix, writes manifest.json last, and a prefix-scoped B2 Event Notification starts downstream processing.

- **Audience:** Drone program and field operations leads, Survey, inspection and mapping data engineers, Security and records owners
- **Problem:** Drone teams collect data on SD cards spread across field crews and docks. They need a resumable, verifiable offload into one durable place, with chain of custody and a reliable processing trigger, without running a file server.
- **Workflow:** rclone copy (native B2 backend, checksum verified) moves SD-card or staging folders into `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/`; a browser field portal can upload stills with presigned PUT URLs → Multi-GB video uses multipart upload, because a single PUT is capped at 5 GB → The uploader writes manifest.json last with mission, site, aircraft, camera, CRS and a file list with client-computed hashes → A B2 Event Notification rule on the raw/ prefix posts to an event broker, which ignores everything except */manifest.json before enqueuing jobs → A lifecycle rule cancels unfinished large-file uploads; raw captures are never moved or tiered → Object Lock retention or a legal hold protects raw captures kept as evidence → Vendor-cloud fleets (DJI Dock, FlightHub) land in the vendor cloud first; an rclone relay copies them to B2
- **Expected scale:** Bursty uploads after each flight, sized from image count, video bitrate and duration, and telemetry frequency. Standard B2 is the default; offload speed is usually bounded by the field uplink. Use rclone or SDK multipart concurrency for large video.

## [Reconstruct orthomosaics, elevation models, point clouds and meshes from mission imagery](../architectures/photogrammetry-processing/architecture.md)

Stateless CPU/GPU workers pull a mission's raw images from B2, run SfM/MVS with OpenDroneMap NodeODM or COLMAP on local NVMe scratch, and write orthomosaic, DSM/DTM, LAZ point cloud, textured mesh and quality report to an immutable per-run prefix.

- **Audience:** Photogrammetry and GIS processing engineers, Survey and construction technology teams, Platform engineers running GPU or CPU batch compute
- **Problem:** Teams reprocess missions when parameters or software change. They need inputs and every run's outputs kept side by side without a shared filesystem tying compute to storage.
- **Workflow:** An event or an operator triggers a job for `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/` → The worker downloads images to local NVMe scratch and submits them to NodeODM (pyodm) or runs pycolmap → NodeODM uploads task-ID results to a dedicated client staging bucket with no key-prefix restriction; the publisher reads staging and writes the versioned products/ layout → Or the worker writes outputs with boto3 managed multipart to `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/` → A run manifest.json records software versions, parameters, the input manifest hash and output keys; new run ids keep earlier runs immutable → Desktop tools without S3 support (Agisoft Metashape, PIX4Dmatic) are staged with rclone into the same layout → The run manifest landing triggers COG conversion, point cloud tiling and AI inspection
- **Expected scale:** Storage and scratch requirements depend on the image set, output formats, and reconstruction settings. Standard B2 is the default; workers are compute-bound. Keep SfM scratch on local NVMe and upload only finished products.

## [Serve orthomosaics and elevation models as cloud-optimized map layers](../architectures/cog-map-serving/architecture.md)

Orthomosaics, DEMs and index maps such as NDVI are converted to Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs in `cog/<mission-id>/` and read in place by TiTiler, QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, GeoServer and rasterio through HTTP range requests, with CDN or presigned client delivery and no stored tile pyramid.

- **Audience:** GIS and web-mapping engineers, Survey, agriculture and construction analytics teams, Client-delivery and platform engineers
- **Problem:** Clients and analysts need to view and analyze multi-GB orthomosaics and DEMs without downloading them, and providers do not want to pre-render and store a second XYZ tile copy of every mission.
- **Workflow:** A conversion job reads `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/orthophoto.tif` and writes a COG with internal overviews to `cog/<mission-id>/<product>.tif` through GDAL /vsis3/ (rio-cogeo or gdal_translate -of COG) → TiTiler renders XYZ/WMTS tiles on demand from range GETs and accepts only validated layer ids, never raw URLs → QGIS, ArcGIS Pro and GeoServer open the same objects in place → Optional analytics jobs read only needed windows and write masks and GeoJSON to `analysis/<mission-id>/` → Public basemaps go through Cloudflare with B2 as origin; private deliverables go out as presigned GETs or through a signing Worker
- **Expected scale:** Few large COGs per mission with many small concurrent range reads from viewers and tile servers. Standard B2 behind a CDN or tile cache is the default; tile caches absorb repeated reads. Measure sustained origin read rates before considering Overdrive.

## [Convert point clouds and meshes into streamable 3D datasets for web viewers](../architectures/point-cloud-3d-streaming/architecture.md)

PDAL and Entwine clean, classify and convert photogrammetric and drone-LiDAR point clouds to COPC or EPT on B2 through s3:// paths, meshes and Gaussian splats for site digital twins are versioned alongside, and browser viewers stream them by range request from a public bucket or CDN.

- **Audience:** LiDAR and 3D data engineers, Construction, mining and corridor digital-twin teams, Web 3D viewer developers
- **Problem:** Site and corridor point clouds are too large for clients to download. Teams need range-readable versions next to the source data for digital twins, volume measurement and construction progress.
- **Workflow:** Source LAS/LAZ from NodeODM or a LiDAR payload lands in `pointcloud/<mission-id>/<run-id>/raw/` → A PDAL pipeline filters, classifies and reprojects, reading s3:// input and writing .copc.laz back through Arbiter with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only; Arbiter prepends https://) → For multi-flight or very large sites, Entwine builds an EPT index into `pointcloud/<site>/ept/` through the same Arbiter S3 driver → Digital-twin jobs version camera poses, meshes and .ply splats under `twins/<site>/<capture-id>/` → Viewers (Potree, CesiumJS, COPC viewers) fetch by HTTP URL from a public bucket with CORS or through a CDN or signing Worker → Optionally, the twin is compared against IFC/BIM models to track construction progress
- **Expected scale:** Hundreds of MB to hundreds of GB per site, read by many small range requests from viewers. Standard B2 behind a CDN is the default. Per-file presigned URLs are impractical for multi-file octrees; prefer a CDN or signing Worker.

## [Detect and geolocate defects in inspection imagery and video](../architectures/ai-inspection-detection/architecture.md)

YOLO or Roboflow Inference models scan inspection video and stills of towers, lines, solar farms, blades, bridges and roofs; geotagged detections, annotated keyframes, GeoJSON and Parquet roll-ups land in `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/` and DuckDB queries them in place.

- **Audience:** Energy, utility and infrastructure inspection teams, Computer-vision and MLOps engineers, Asset-management data engineers
- **Problem:** Each inspection video fans out into hundreds of derived objects across thousands of assets per season. Operators need results tied to source media and location, queryable fleet-wide, and reprocessable in batch when models improve.
- **Workflow:** Source video and SRT/GPX telemetry land in raw/ (see flight-capture-offload) and the manifest event enqueues an inference job → The worker streams video from B2, samples keyframes, runs Ultralytics YOLO on a local GPU and extracts the GPS track from sidecar telemetry → It writes annotated keyframes, per-frame detection JSON, summary.json and a GeoJSON track to `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/`; the review UI reads them by presigned GET → Edge variant - Roboflow Inference on a ground station or dock computer archives only flagged frames and prediction JSON, with hourly Parquet roll-ups under summaries/ → DuckDB httpfs with an S3 secret whose ENDPOINT is the B2 endpoint queries detection Parquet fleet-wide and writes slices back to `query-slices/` with COPY → When a better model ships, a batch job reprocesses the archive under a new model-version prefix
- **Expected scale:** Hundreds of derived objects per inspection across thousands of assets per season. Standard B2 is the default. Parquet roll-ups keep fleet-wide queries to a few range reads instead of listing millions of JSON objects.

## [Label inspection frames and publish versioned defect-detection datasets](../architectures/inspection-training-data/architecture.md)

Flagged frames and orthomosaic chips are deduplicated, pre-labeled with SAM 2 or labeled in CVAT or Label Studio directly against B2, and exported as immutable dataset versions under `datasets/<name>/<version>/` next to versioned model checkpoints.

- **Audience:** Computer-vision data and labeling operations teams, MLOps engineers training defect-detection models, Security and storage architects
- **Problem:** Defect classes such as cracks, corrosion, vegetation encroachment and thermal hot spots are rare and site-specific, so teams continuously relabel and retrain. They need labeling tools that read media from the archive without copying it and reproducible dataset versions tied to model versions.
- **Workflow:** A curation job selects candidate frames from inspections/ and chips orthomosaic tiles; fastdup flags duplicates and outliers and quarantines them without deleting → SAM 2 writes pre-labeled masks into a draft label prefix → CVAT attaches B2 as Amazon S3 cloud storage with the B2 Endpoint URL, or Label Studio syncs source storage and writes annotations to target storage through its S3 Endpoint field → Reviewed labels are exported as COCO/YOLO to `datasets/<name>/<version>/` with a manifest of source keys and hashes; versions are never overwritten → Training workers cache shards on local NVMe, write checkpoints to `models/<name>/<version>/` and record the dataset version used → New model versions feed batch reprocessing in ai-inspection-detection
- **Expected scale:** Thousands to millions of frames and chips per dataset version, read repeatedly during training. Standard B2 is the default; cache shards on local NVMe for multi-epoch training. Consider Overdrive only for sustained multi-GPU reads where storage throughput is the measured bottleneck.
